title: A worker agent's own git still inherits the operator's rerere cache
description:
6na disabled rerere on every git the RECONCILER runs. A worker agent's own git — a pull, merge or rebase it runs inside its worktree — shares the same .git/rr-cache and inherits the host's global rerere.enabled=true. So an operator's hand-recorded conflict resolution can be replayed into a worker's tree without the worker choosing it, and without anyone seeing it happen.

That is the same hazard 6na was filed for, one layer out: the tree a worker gates and hands over would be something nobody chose — not the worker's, not the base's, not a reviewer's.

gitbin.WithNoAutoMaintenance already pins agent environments through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT / GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n (tick mel), so the rerere pair can ride the same mechanism in one place rather than becoming a second list of pins.

Watch the interaction with b4r while doing this: the read-only grade lets GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS through, and git applies it AFTER GIT_CONFIG_COUNT — so a pin added here can be overridden by an inherited value until b4r is fixed.

Reported by 6na, run epic-dha, finding e4676545.
acceptance_criteria: A worker agent's git cannot read or write the host's rerere cache, pinned through the same environment mechanism as the maintenance settings, with a test that sets rerere.enabled globally and proves a worker's merge still conflicts
